To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) self-control mechanisms are more important than formal control modes to increase platform stickiness; (2) self-control mechanisms positively affect developers’ perceived autonomy; (3) perceived autonomy fully mediates the relationship between control mechanisms and platform stickiness.

self-control plays an important role in increasing developers’ intention to stick with a platform, and that the relationship between formal and informal control modes and stickiness is fully explained by perceived autonomy.

self-control is more effective in increasing platform stickness than formal control mechanisms, and that the relationship between both formal and self-control modes and platform stickness is fully mediated by the perceived autonomy of third-party developers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of control modes on third-party developers’ stickiness to a software-based platform, which is a novel and important research topic in the context of platform-based software development.
how control mechanisms influence third-party developers' intention to stick with a platform.
the role of control mechanisms for thirdparty developers’ intentions to continue to use a mobile app developmentplatform, and how this role is mediated by developers’ perceptions of autonomy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-determination, self-regulation, and the perceived autonomy of third-party developers are key factors for platform stickiness.
self-control is a more powerful mechanism to influence the intention to stay with a platform than output and process control.

the more a platform owner is able to create and maintain a sense of belonging and autonomy in the minds of developers, the more likely it is that the platform owner will be able to retain them in the long run.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

self-control mechanisms, such as the freedom to choose the platform, and the autonomy to develop and sell apps are more important than formal control mechanisms, such as output control (e.g., app sales) and process control (e.g. development time) in increasing platform stick-iness.
the more a developer perceives to be able to control the process, the higher is the likelihood to stick with a platform.
self-control mechanisms have a stronger influence on developers’ platform stickiness than formal control mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
platform providers should focus on self-determination and autonomy of developers to keep them engaged with the platform.
platform owners can benefit from a more self-determination oriented platform governance, which is based on self-regulation and autonomy-supportive control mechanisms.
platform owners should focus on the self-determination needs of their developers, rather than on hierarchical control, if they want to keep their developers on board.
